title: feat: support GPT-5.6 Ultra across OpenClaw and Codex runtimes

commit.messageHeadline: feat: support GPT-5.6 Ultra across agent runtimes
fix(codex): mirror V2 native subagent tasks
chore: refresh plugin SDK surface budgets
test: expose Ultra wire effort proof
test(cron): avoid hoisted mock initialization race

Codex review: needs maintainer review before merge. _Reviewed July 10, 2026, 10:15 AM ET / 14:15 UTC._

**Summary**
The branch adds canonical GPT-5.6 Ultra reasoning, runtime-aware model/thinking selection and persistence, Codex V2 subagent task mirroring, fresh OpenAI defaults, and corresponding channel, Gateway, TUI, web UI, plugin, documentation, and live-test support.

Reproducibility: not applicable. This PR introduces a cross-runtime feature rather than fixing one narrowly reproducible current-main bug; the high-confidence verification path is its live embedded and native Codex scenarios plus focused persistence and switching tests.

**Review metrics:** 2 noteworthy metrics.
- **Fresh setup defaults:** 2 changed. API-key and Codex/OAuth onboarding now choose distinct GPT-5.6 refs, so fresh-install behavior needs explicit maintainer acceptance while upgrades preserve stored choices.
- **Plugin SDK surface:** 2 public exports, 1 callable export added. Effective agent-runtime resolution becomes a supported external plugin seam rather than an internal implementation detail.

**Stored data model**
Persistent data-model change detected: `serialized state: src/gateway/session-event-payload.ts`, `serialized state: src/gateway/session-utils.test.ts`, `serialized state: src/gateway/session-utils.ts`, `serialized state: src/gateway/session-utils.types.ts`, `serialized state: src/gateway/sessions-patch.test.ts`, `serialized state: src/gateway/sessions-patch.ts`, and 16 more. Confirm migration or upgrade compatibility proof before merge.

**Root-cause cluster**
Relationship: `fixed_by_candidate`
Canonical: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/98296
Summary: This PR is the implementation candidate for the Ultra and runtime-coherence work explicitly separated from the GPT-5.6 family umbrella; the other linked PRs address narrower adjacent reasoning/provider boundaries.

Members:
- `canonical`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/98296 - The umbrella explicitly states that native Ultra orchestration remains separate work in this PR.
- `partial_overlap`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/90703 - Both use provider compatibility metadata for extended reasoning efforts, but that PR does not implement GPT-5.6 runtime switching, persistence, or native Codex lifecycle behavior.
- `adjacent_distinct`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95852 - That PR fixes inherited ACP model leakage into the Codex thinking slot through a separate runtime and persistence path.
- `adjacent_distinct`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/80033 - That PR advertises DeepSeek V4 effort metadata for one provider and does not implement GPT-5.6 Ultra semantics.
- `adjacent_distinct`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/77423 - The merged OpenRouter fix establishes the provider wire-effort boundary that this PR preserves when lowering unsupported logical Ultra.

Proposal only: this assessment does not dispatch repair, suppress jobs, mutate sibling items, close, or merge anything.

**Merge readiness**
Overall: 🦞 diamond lobster
Proof: 🦀 challenger crab ✨ media proof bonus
Patch quality: 🦞 diamond lobster
Result: ready for maintainer review.

Overall follows the weaker of proof and patch quality, so missing proof can cap an otherwise strong patch.

**Mantis proof suggestion**
Native Telegram proof would materially confirm that runtime-aware Ultra choices are visible only where supported; it is supplemental because the PR already has strong live runtime proof. A maintainer can ask Mantis to capture proof by posting this exact PR comment:

```text
@openclaw-mantis telegram desktop proof: verify that /think shows Ultra for OpenClaw GPT-5.6 Luna but not native Codex Luna, and return a redacted recording or screenshots.
```

**Risk before merge**
- [P1] Fresh API-key setup now selects `openai/gpt-5.6`, while fresh Codex/OAuth setup selects exact `openai/gpt-5.6-sol`; the tests preserve existing explicit choices, but maintainers must intentionally accept these new onboarding defaults.
- [P1] The canonical thinking contract and Plugin SDK gain runtime-aware Ultra behavior plus new public exports, creating a long-lived compatibility surface for external plugins and provider capability metadata.
- [P2] Persisted model, runtime, and thinking state now participate together in fallback, reconnect reconciliation, session patching, UI merges, heartbeat/cron execution, and Codex V1/V2 thread rotation; the proof is strong, but a regression in these invariants could stale or mis-associate session behavior.
- [P1] The current head was mergeable but behind current base and still had two exact-head checks in progress at review time; refresh/merge validation must use the final three-way result and exact head.

**Maintainer options:**
1. **Land the tested contract (recommended)**  
   Accept the fresh defaults, additive Plugin SDK seam, and persisted runtime/thinking behavior after exact-head CI and maintainer review.
2. **Split durable contract changes**  
   Remove the fresh-default changes or public SDK export and land the runtime/Codex mechanics in a narrower patch.
3. **Pause the preview feature**  
   Keep the PR open if maintainers are not ready to establish GPT-5.6 preview defaults and Ultra contracts.

**Next step before merge**
- [P2] No narrow automated repair remains; the maintainer should decide whether to accept the fresh defaults and permanent plugin/provider/session contract, then finish exact-head merge validation.

**Maintainer decision needed**
- Question: Should OpenClaw adopt this combined GPT-5.6 Ultra contract now, including the two fresh-setup default changes and the additive public runtime-resolution Plugin SDK seam?
- Rationale: The patch is technically sound and matches Codex, but onboarding defaults and external plugin/provider contracts are durable product choices that cannot be inferred from tests alone.
- Likely owner: steipete — The PR is assigned to steipete, who authored and integrated the current product-scope branch and has the strongest evidence of ownership over the decision surface.
- Options:
  - **Adopt the combined contract (recommended):** Land the full runtime, persistence, fresh-default, and additive SDK behavior after exact-head checks and merge refresh pass.
  - **Narrow before landing:** Keep the runtime and Codex lifecycle work but defer either the fresh defaults or public SDK export to a separately approved change.
  - **Pause preview adoption:** Keep the PR open until GPT-5.6 preview availability and permanent Ultra semantics are clearer.

**Security**
Cleared: No concrete security or supply-chain regression was found; the workflow changes add repository-owned live suites without new third-party action refs, dependency sources, executable downloads, secret scopes, or permission expansion.

Adopt the single runtime-aware thinking and session contract as one coherent implementation if maintainers approve the new onboarding defaults and public SDK seam; preserve existing explicit user selections, keep provider wire lowering capability-gated and non-escalating, and require exact-head CI/merge validation before landing.

Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue?

Not applicable. This PR introduces a cross-runtime feature rather than fixing one narrowly reproducible current-main bug; the high-confidence verification path is its live embedded and native Codex scenarios plus focused persistence and switching tests.

Is this the best way to solve the issue?

Yes for the implementation shape: resolving the effective agent runtime once and carrying that prepared fact through provider policy, validation, persistence, and UI projection is more maintainable than channel-specific inference or a generic `ultra -> max` alias. The new onboarding defaults and public SDK exposure still require explicit maintainer product acceptance.

- **Current branch shape:** The live head is six focused commits directly atop current main; the newest commit only fixes a hoisted cron test mock and does not change the previously reviewed runtime feature. ([`src/cron/isolated-agent/run.test-harness.ts:1`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3faec2226160/src/cron/isolated-agent/run.test-harness.ts#L1), [3faec2226160](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/3faec2226160))
- **Canonical runtime resolution:** The branch introduces one effective-runtime resolver that applies session overrides before model/provider harness policy and resolves automatic selection without triggering discovery, then carries that runtime into thinking validation. ([`src/agents/thinking-runtime.ts:17`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/4195656fae16/src/agents/thinking-runtime.ts#L17), [4195656fae16](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/4195656fae16))
- **Runtime-aware OpenAI policy:** The OpenAI thinking profile uses runtime plus authoritative compatibility metadata to distinguish embedded logical Ultra from native Codex model support, avoiding a generic provider-wide alias. ([`extensions/openai/thinking-policy.ts:53`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/4195656fae16/extensions/openai/thinking-policy.ts#L53), [4195656fae16](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/4195656fae16))
- **Codex V2 task bridge:** OpenClaw accepts only the authoritative completed `subAgentActivity` item, registers its child thread, and mirrors it into the shared task lifecycle while preserving parent scoping and deduplication. ([`extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-subagent-task-mirror.ts:76`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ed1d6b384e32/extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-subagent-task-mirror.ts#L76), [ed1d6b384e32](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/ed1d6b384e32))
- **Codex thread compatibility:** The branch rotates a native Codex thread only when switching between the GPT-5.6 V2 family (Sol/Terra) and V1 Luna, while allowing Sol/Terra switches to resume the existing compatible thread. ([`extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.ts:440`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/4195656fae16/extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.ts#L440), [4195656fae16](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/4195656fae16))
- **Upstream Ultra contract:** Current upstream Codex defines `ReasoningEffort::Ultra`, serializes it as `ultra`, and parses that literal, supporting the native app-server payload used by this PR. ([`../codex/codex-rs/protocol/src/openai_models.rs:40`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/c0b85c96d981/../codex/codex-rs/protocol/src/openai_models.rs#L40), [c0b85c96d981](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/c0b85c96d981))
